prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map separates the near countertop and the camera wearer’s hands/cloth from the farther blue wall and cabinets: the counter is roughly 0.3–0.8 m away, while the wall is about 1–2 m away, although monocular depth does not provide reliable metric scale. Bottles and fruit remain clustered on the far edge of the counter, roughly 0.6–1.0 m from the wearer and within about 0.1–0.4 m of one another; the cooktop and pans lie to their left at similar depth. Across frames 1–3 the viewpoint stays over the counter, then turns left/downward in frames 4–5, bringing the hands or foreground edge very near and shifting the cooktop toward the center; no separate person is visible. Bright foreground regions clarify reach and occlusion beyond RGB, but clipped white areas, blurred boundaries, and inconsistent brightness around the counter, hands, and reflective pans make exact distances and overlap ordering unreliable.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates several bottles and the banana cluster along the rear of the counter in frames 1–3, showing that these are separate adjacent objects about 0.6–1.0 m from the wearer and mostly within a few tenths of a metre of each other. In frame 4 it additionally marks a bowl-like object and a mouse-like object to the left of the bottle group, plus the camera wearer’s hand-held phone and a partial person mask low in the frame; these foreground masks overlap, indicating occlusion and proximity within arm’s reach. By frame 5 most objects have moved outside the field of view as the camera turns, leaving only a partly cropped bottle at the far right; no other person is identified, so facing direction or gaze of another person cannot be established. The map makes object separation and partial visibility clearer than RGB, but several labels appear unreliable—especially “mouse,” “cell phone,” “bowl,” and the fragmented person mask—and it misses large objects such as the counter, cloth, pans, and most of the wearer’s hands.
descriptions.pose: The pose map detects only small magenta hand skeletons, with one cluster in frame 2 and another in frame 3, positioned low-left within those frames where the wearer’s hands grasp the cloth over the counter. These detections place the hands roughly 0.3–0.6 m from the camera and within arm’s reach, but no yellow body skeleton or complete person pose appears in any frame, so body orientation, facing direction, and gaze cannot be determined. The hand location shifts from farther left in frame 2 to nearer the center-left in frame 3, consistent with relative hand or camera movement before the viewpoint turns in frames 4–5; the hands then become undetected despite remaining partly visible in RGB. The map can expose articulated hand location against clutter more clearly than RGB, but its sparse, intermittent detections and absent limbs make occlusion, exact joint geometry, inter-person distance, and approach or retreat unreliable.
